newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schickedanz, Karstadt seek strategic alliance.
newsitem.headline: Schickedanz, Karstadt seek strategic alliance.

text.p: German retail group Schickedanz could eventually increase its stake in Karstadt from the initial 20.3 percent as part of a strategic alliance, a Schickedanz spokesman said on Tuesday.
The two companies first said late on Monday that Schickedanz would buy the 20.3 percent stake from Commerzbank AG and Deutsche Bank AG.
The price of the stake was not given, but insiders estimated it at up to 1.3 billion marks.

Karstadt chairman Walter Deuss welcomed the investment from Schickedanz, which is a subsidiary of the Quelle group, and said the two would cooperate in purchasing abroad and in developing internet sales.
Deuss said in a television interview he sees Schickedanz as a serious shareholder.
The Schickedanz spokesman said the two enterprises have a great deal in common, but he declined to give details of their plans for the future. "We are just at the start of the process," he said.
The two could easily cooperate in shipping and in catalogue sales, where Karstadt is active through its unit Neckarmann. But the cartel authorities' view is an open question.
A spokeswoman for the cartel office said it would not take a position for the time being. The investment would not be regarded as a merger unless Schickedanz raised its stake to 25 percent.

But cartel authorities could act sooner if one of the two parties were seen as having a determining role in a particular market and if this position were strengthened through the alliance, the spokeswoman said.
Schickedanz said the group's investments would be more strongly oriented toward market position and profitability.
Schickedanz chairman Steffen Stremme said in May the Quelle group would seek to overcome its growth and profit problems through new organisation, specialisation and internationalisation.
Schickedanz, with 33,000 employees, had sales of 14.2 billion marks in the year to January 31, 1997, of which 12 billion marks came from catalogue sales.
Karstadt, with 100,000 employees, had 1996 sales of 27 billion marks.
